title: Fishing for Magikarp: Automatically Detecting Under-trained Tokens in Large Lang
reason: Main contribution is detecting glitch (under-trained) tokens in LLM tokenizer vocabularies, an explicit in-scope topic.

title: Tokenization as Finite-State Transduction
reason: Main contribution is a formal theory of BPE and WordPiece tokenization as finite-state transduction.

title: MonoByte: A Pool of Monolingual Byte-level Language Models
reason: Main contribution is a pool of pretrained models released as a resource for cross-lingual transfer research; byte-level input is chosen to remove a confound, not studied as the topic.

title: Temperature-scaling surprisal estimates improve fit to human reading times -- bu
reason: Main topic is psycholinguistic surprisal calibration and reading times; multi-subword words appear only as a side finding.

title: An In-depth Study on Internal Structure of Chinese Words
reason: Main contribution is a word-internal dependency treebank and parsing task for syntactic parsing, not tokenization for a neural LM or MT system.

title: Finite-context Indexing of Restricted Output Space for NLP Models Facing Noisy I
reason: Main contribution is a noise-sanitization (spelling-correction style) front end for noisy input; tokenization is not the topic.

title: DARTFormer: Finding The Best Type Of Attention
reason: Main contribution is neural architecture search over attention types; byte-level text classification is only a benchmark task.

title: Extreme Model Compression for On-device Natural Language Understanding
reason: Main contribution is word-embedding compression for on-device NLU; vocabulary size is a setting, not the studied choice.

title: Comparing Neural- and N-Gram-Based Language Models for Word Segmentation
reason: Classical word segmentation (inserting word boundaries) aimed at a microtext normalization preprocessing step, not at neural LM or MT input; the character-level LM is a tool inside the segmenter.
disagreement_note: The borderline rule admits classical word segmentation only when it is aimed at neural LM or MT input, and this system targets microtext normalization; but word segmentation is close enough to the topic that this is a judgement call, so I defer to the author.

title: Noisy Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for Code LLMs
reason: Main contribution is a test-time RL framework for code LLM robustness; character-level perturbations are only part of the benchmark.

title: Integrating Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory with Subword Embedding for Auth
reason: Main contribution is a BLSTM+CNN authorship attribution model that uses subword embeddings as a tool; the tokenizer itself is not studied.
disagreement_note: The decision rule says using subwords as a tool is not enough; the paper's topic is authorship attribution and no tokenization choice is built, compared or measured. Override.

title: Morphological Typology in BPE Subword Productivity and Language Modeling
reason: Main analysis is how morphological typology affects BPE tokenization and the resulting language-modeling performance.

title: The Meaning Factory at SemEval-2017 Task 9: Producing AMRs with Neural Semantic
reason: Shared-task system paper that uses a character-based seq2seq model as a tool for AMR parsing; the input-unit choice is not the studied topic.
disagreement_note: The boundary states that a paper that merely uses a character-level model for some task is out; this is an AMR semantic parsing system description. Override.

title: VEPO: Variable Entropy Policy Optimization for Low-Resource Language Foundation
reason: Main contribution is an RL policy-optimization method (RLVR with variable entropy); subword segmentation is cited as motivation and 'tokenization efficiency' as an outcome, but no tokenizer is built or analysed.
disagreement_note: A reader would describe the topic as RL alignment for low-resource MT, not tokenization, but the abstract is vague about how tokenization efficiency improves, so this is a judgement call; defer to the author.

title: HarperValleyBank: A Domain-Specific Spoken Dialog Corpus
reason: Spoken dialog corpus release; 'vocabulary size' refers to the number of unique words in the data, not a neural tokenizer.

title: A Joint Model for Word Embedding and Word Morphology
reason: Unsupervised morpheme segmentation learned jointly with a word-embedding (skip-gram style) model, which the boundary lists among embedding/classical models rather than neural LM or MT input.
disagreement_note: The out-of-scope list names word-level vocabularies of embedding models, yet the paper's core is a learned subword segmentation of words for a neural embedding model, which many readers would count as early subword work; judgement call, defer to the author.

title: MeshAnything V2: Artist-Created Mesh Generation With Adjacent Mesh Tokenization
reason: Tokenization of 3D meshes (vertices and faces), which is non-text tokenization.
disagreement_note: The boundary explicitly excludes non-text tokenizers (image, molecule, DNA 'or other non-text tokenization'); mesh tokenization falls under that exclusion. Override.

title: ByT5: Towards a token-free future with pre-trained byte-to-byte models
reason: The paper's point is bytes versus subword tokens as the input unit for a pretrained LM, named explicitly in the boundary.

title: Unsupervised End-to-End Learning of Discrete Linguistic Units for Voice Conversi
reason: Discrete units discovered from speech audio for voice conversion; speech tokenization is excluded.

title: Tokenization Matters! Degrading Large Language Models through Challenging Their
reason: Main contribution is an adversarial dataset that attacks LLM token segmentation and measures the resulting degradation (tokenizer robustness and security).

title: Natural Language Processing: A Comprehensive Practical Guide from Tokenisation t
reason: A practicum covering the whole NLP pipeline (fine-tuning, RAG, RLHF, agents, multimodal); tokenisation is one session among seventeen, so the main topic is not tokenization.
disagreement_note: Surveys are in scope only when they survey the tokenization topics; the decision rule requires that a reader would describe the main topic as tokenization, and here it is general NLP education. Override.

title: Efficient Domain Adaptation for Text Line Recognition via Decoupled Language Mod
reason: Main contribution is a modular OCR detection-and-correction framework; ByT5 versus T5 is an architecture-selection finding inside an OCR paper, not the studied topic.

title: CANINE: Pre-training an Efficient Tokenization-Free Encoder for Language Represe
reason: The paper's point is a character-level, tokenization-free encoder as an alternative to subword vocabularies; CANINE is named in the boundary as in scope.
disagreement_note: The boundary lists CANINE by name under in-scope byte/character/tokenizer-free models, and the abstract frames the contribution around removing the tokenization step and fixed vocabulary. Override.

title: Comparison of Current Approaches to Lemmatization: A Case Study in Estonian
reason: Lemmatization comparison that uses a character-level generative model as one approach; tokenization is not the topic.

title: FOUNDv2: Learning Unified User Quantized Tokenizers for User Representation
reason: RQ-VAE quantized tokenizer for heterogeneous user behaviour data, which is non-text tokenization.
disagreement_note: The boundary excludes VQ-VAE style and other non-text tokenizers; user-behaviour data is not text for a language model or MT system. Override.

title: Multi-level biomedical NER through multi-granularity embeddings and enhanced lab
reason: Biomedical NER system that adds a character-level CNN to BERT embeddings; character-level information is used as a tool, not studied as the input-unit choice.
disagreement_note: The decision rule says using subwords or character features as a tool is not enough, and the paper's topic is biomedical NER. Override.

title: Echoes Across Vietnam's Highlands, Delta, and Coast: A Multilingual Corpus for C
reason: Main contribution is a corpus and benchmark for three minority languages; vocabulary augmentation and fragmentation are part of the adaptation recipe but not the paper's main topic.

title: A Family of LLMs Liberated from Static Vocabularies
reason: Main contribution is byte-level tokenizer-free (HAT) LLMs presented as a replacement for fixed-vocabulary tokenizers, with compression and robustness measured.

title: Enhancing Robustness of Autoregressive Language Models against Orthographic Atta
reason: The paper's point is replacing subword tokenizer embeddings with pixel-rendered input units to fix the tokenizer's out-of-vocabulary weakness, i.e. the choice of input unit for an LM.

title: MDM-Prime-v2: Binary Encoding and Index Shuffling Enable Scaling of Diffusion La
reason: The 'subtokenizer' is a binary index encoding of BPE token ids inside a masked diffusion LM, and the main topic is scaling diffusion language models rather than how text is split into tokens.

title: How does a Language-Specific Tokenizer affect LLMs?
reason: Main analysis is tokenizer extension for Korean and its measured effect on LLM behaviour (tokenizer adaptation to a new language).

title: ESCELL: Emergent Symbolic Cellular Language
reason: Emergent communication between agents in a referential game over cell images; 'vocabulary size' is the symbol set of the game, not a text tokenizer.

title: PhishKey: A Novel Centroid-Based Approach for Enhanced Phishing Detection Using
reason: Phishing detection system that uses a character-level CNN on URLs as a tool; tokenization is not the topic.

title: The Evolution of Multimodal Model Architectures
reason: Survey of multimodal architecture types; the 'tokenizers' discussed are multimodal input tokenizers and the text tokenizer itself is not studied.

title: Shorthand for Thought: Compressing LLM Reasoning via Entropy-Guided Supertokens
reason: Main contribution is extending the model's vocabulary with cross-word BPE supertokens learned from reasoning traces and measuring the effect on reasoning length and accuracy (vocabulary extension and tokenization effects on reasoning), not post-hoc prompt compression.

title: Uzbek Cyrillic-Latin-Cyrillic Machine Transliteration
reason: Script transliteration with a decision-tree classifier; no neural LM or MT tokenizer is built or evaluated.

title: Faster Superword Tokenization
reason: Main contribution is a faster training algorithm for the BoundlessBPE and SuperBPE subword tokenization algorithms.

title: SCRIPT: A Subcharacter Compositional Representation Injection Module for Korean
reason: Proposes an embedding-injection module that adds Jamo subcharacter features to existing subword embeddings without changing the tokenizer, so the main contribution is a representation module rather than how text is split; in doubt, out.

title: FourierQK: Filter Shape, Admissibility and the Leakage-Coverage Law
reason: Attention filter-shape ablation that uses character-level language modelling only as a testbed; tokenization is not the topic.

title: Fine-Grained Address Segmentation for Attention-Based Variable-Degree Prefetchin
reason: Segmentation of memory addresses for hardware prefetching, which is non-text tokenization outside language modelling.

title: MultiTok: Variable-Length Tokenization for Efficient LLMs Adapted from LZW Compr
reason: Main contribution is a new LZW-inspired text tokenization method for LLM training and its measured effect on training efficiency and accuracy.

title: Downstream Task-Oriented Neural Tokenizer Optimization with Vocabulary Restricti
reason: Main contribution is a method to optimize tokenization (a BiLSTM tokenizer with vocabulary restriction) for downstream neural models.

title: Patching Leaks in the Charformer for Efficient Character-Level Generation
reason: The paper's point is character-level versus subword input for NMT, fixing Charformer's character-grouping (GBST) so it works in the decoder and measuring translation quality and speed.

title: A Voice-Interactive Multi-Agent System for Smart Operating Rooms: Architecture D
reason: LLM agent system for operating rooms; KV-cache prefix reuse and context-window management are excluded topics and tokenization is not studied.

title: Innovative tokenisation of structured data for LLM training
reason: Tokenisation scheme for tabular NetFlow network-flow records (structured non-text data) for an intrusion-detection foundation model, which falls under non-text tokenization; in doubt, out.

title: On the Effect of (Near) Duplicate Subwords in Language Modelling
reason: Main analysis is how near-duplicate subwords in the tokenizer vocabulary affect LM training efficiency (evaluation of tokenization).

title: CAD-Tokenizer: Towards Text-based CAD Prototyping via Modality-Specific Tokeniza
reason: VQ-VAE tokenizer for CAD construction sequences, which is non-text modality tokenization.

title: Tokenizer Fertility and Zero-Shot Performance of Foundation Models on Ukrainian
reason: Headline analysis measures tokenizer fertility and token cost across foundation models on Ukrainian text (multilingual fertility and cost), although half of the findings concern zero-shot task performance.

title: Let's Fuse Step by Step: A Generative Fusion Decoding Algorithm with LLMs for Ro
reason: Main contribution is a shallow-fusion decoding algorithm for ASR and OCR; byte-level likelihood is a mechanism to bridge mismatched token spaces, not the studied topic.

title: SubRegWeigh: Effective and Efficient Annotation Weighing with Subword Regulariza
reason: Uses subword regularization as a tool to detect annotation errors; the tokenization technique itself is not the contribution.

title: Benchmarking Document Parsers on Mathematical Formula Extraction from PDFs
reason: Benchmark of PDF formula parsers; 'character-level matching' is an evaluation metric, not tokenization for a neural LM.

title: Evolving Character-Level DenseNet Architectures using Genetic Programming
reason: Evolutionary architecture search for character-level CNNs on text classification; the character-level model is used as a tool and the input-unit choice is not studied.

title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
reason: Main contribution is a recipe for expanding a pretrained LLM's BPE tokenizer to new languages and measuring fertility and decode-cost gains (tokenizer extension and adaptation).

title: Improved Learned Sparse Retrieval with Corpus-Specific Vocabularies
reason: Main analysis is the choice of a corpus-specific BERT token vocabulary and its size, with measured effects on retrieval effectiveness and latency (vocabulary size and domain adaptation of a neural model's tokenizer).

title: Flexibly Scaling Large Language Models Contexts Through Extensible Tokenization
reason: Despite the name, 'Extensible Tokenization' compresses token embeddings to extend the context window, which is context compression and excluded.

title: Evaluating Byte and Wordpiece Level Models for Massively Multilingual Semantic P
reason: The paper's framing is a comparison of byte-level (ByT5) versus wordpiece (mT5) input units across 51 languages, i.e. the input-unit choice is the studied variable, although label projection and synthetic data take up much of the work.

title: MoVoC: Morphology-Aware Subword Construction for Geez Script Languages
reason: Main contribution is a morpheme-aware subword vocabulary construction method and tokenizer evaluated with intrinsic metrics and MT quality.

title: Morphology Matters: A Multilingual Language Modeling Analysis
reason: Main analysis is how morphology affects LM difficulty under BPE segmentation and shows that linguistically motivated subword segmentation (Morfessor, FSTs) changes it, a measured consequence of the segmentation choice.

title: MOROCO: The Moldavian and Romanian Dialectal Corpus
reason: Dialect corpus release with a character-level CNN baseline used as a tool; tokenization is not the topic.

title: HoloByte: Continuous Hyperspherical Distillation for Tokenizer-Free Modeling
reason: The paper's point is a tokenizer-free byte-level modeling framework proposed as a replacement for subword (BPE) tokenization and compared against a BPE baseline.
